title: Authentication, TLS Verification and Debug Configuration Static Analysis Rules

rules.name: TLS certificate verification disabled
rules.description: An HTTP client call sets verify=False, or ssl._create_unverified_context() / ssl._create_default_https_context is used to build an unverified context. The client then accepts any certificate, so a network attacker can impersonate the server and read or modify the traffic.
rules.remediation_example: requests.get(url, timeout=10)  # keep verification on; install the proper CA bundle instead

rules.name: JWT decoded without signature verification
rules.description: jwt.decode() is called with options={'verify_signature': False} or verify=False. The token payload is accepted without checking its signature, so any caller can forge claims such as an administrator role by writing their own token.

rules.name: Production debug mode enabled
rules.description: DEBUG is assigned True, or a development server (Flask app.run, Django runserver equivalent) is started with debug=True. Debug mode exposes interactive traceback consoles and configuration values, so an unauthenticated visitor can often execute code.
rules.remediation_example: app.run(host='127.0.0.1', debug=False)  # or serve via a production WSGI server
